nodes.name: Get Pipeline Stage
nodes.notes: CRM posts here. Body: lead_id, name, email, company, pipeline_stage. Header auth required.

nodes.name: Normalise Lead
nodes.notes: Trims every field, lower-cases the email, and decides in one place whether the lead is usable.

nodes.name: Check if Contacted
nodes.notes: Usable: has a lead id, a real-looking email, and is in the Contacted stage.

nodes.name: Record Rejected Lead
nodes.notes: A malformed CRM payload leaves a row saying why it was refused - and if that row cannot be written, you are told.

nodes.name: Seen This Lead Before
nodes.notes: Asks the sheet whether this lead already has a row. alwaysOutputData so "not found" is an empty item rather than a stopped branch.

nodes.name: New Lead Only
nodes.notes: True means no row exists yet, so this is a new lead. A CRM retry finds its own row and goes down the false branch.

nodes.name: Record Duplicate Lead
nodes.notes: Makes the discard visible, so a re-sent lead that does nothing can be explained.

nodes.name: Put the Details in DB
nodes.notes: One row per lead. Not retried: a lost response on a retried append writes the lead twice.

parameters.content:
## STAGE 1: Collect leads in the Contacted stage

The CRM posts a lead. It is trimmed and validated, refused with a reason if it is not usable,
and checked against every lead seen before so a CRM retry cannot email anyone twice.
An agent writes the welcome email, a guard refuses to send it if it came back empty,
and the Gmail thread id and message id are stored on the row.

## STAGE 2: Follow up with leads who have not replied

Two days later the thread is read. A reply hands the lead to the team and stops here.
Silence sends a follow-up as a real reply inside the same conversation.

A reply means any inbound message from the lead. Our own sends and bounce notices do not count.
An out-of-office DOES count as a reply, by choice: a person looks at it instead of a robot emailing again.

## STAGE 3: Close the loop on non-responsive leads

Two more days, the same test. Still nothing: a short, warm close saying we will stop emailing
and they are welcome back any time. Not Interested is a resting state, not a dead end.

## When something breaks

Every error output lands here. The row is marked FAILED with the reason and the team is emailed.
A lead that stops halfway has usually already received an email, so the alert says so.

**Alerts go to your-email@example.com.**

## Unsubscribe

Every prospect email carries a link to the top row. The link only shows a page, because link
scanners fetch every URL in an email before the human sees it. The button posts to the row below,
which writes the person onto the Unsubscribed tab.

That tab is checked before the first email and again after every wait, so an opt-out stops the
sequence wherever it has got to - and stops it again if the CRM re-imports the same person later.
